name: Sprint task cards
description:
The user requested five enhancements to the sprint board task cards and creation flow in codx-junior-ui.

I explored the kanban board components (`SprintTaskCard.vue`, `SprintBoardModals.vue`, `SprintBoardView.vue`) and the relevant stores (kanban, chats, users, projects) to understand existing patterns.

I proposed changes to display pending messages, message count, and relative last-update time directly on each task card.

I added a ProjectDetailt selector, recent-profile avatar quick picks, multi-user assignment, and deadline input to the New Task modal.

Task metadata (`project_id`, `users`, `deadline`) is persisted via `$storex.chats.updateChatInfo` after `newSprintTask`, with full Vue components and change summary tables provided.

messages.content:
Tasks:
 - We must show more info in the task cards: pending messages, number of messages, last update time (from now)
 - When creating new task we'll add ProjectDetailt selector to assign a project to the task.
 - When creating new task show recent profiles used in other task as quick selector in an avatar list
 - Allow to assig task to one or more users
 - Allow to set a deadline for the task

I'll analyze the project structure and existing components before proposing changes. Let me explore the relevant areas. ``` Search completed: 5 queries executed, 50 documents found ``` Let me examine the kanban store, the canvas component, and the selectors. ``` Read 5 file(s) | Successfully read: src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardCanvas.vue, src/store/kanban.js, src/components/chat/Selector.vue, src/components/chat/UserSelector.vue, src/components/ProjectDetailt.vue ``` ``` Search completed: 5 queries executed, 50 documents found ``` Let me look at the board folder and the task card components. ``` Search completed: 5 queries executed, 50 documents found ``` Let me read the board column and task card components, plus the chats store fully. ``` Read 2 file(s) | Successfully read: src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardColumn.vue, src/store/chats.js | Failed to read 1 file(s): src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardTaskCard.vue ``` ``` Read 4 file(s) | Successfully read: src/components/kanban/board/SprintTaskCard.vue, src/components/profile/ProfileAvatar.vue, src/components/ProfileCard.vue, src/components/Modal.vue ``` ``` Search completed: 5 queries executed, 50 documents found ``` Let me search for the planning store, unread/pending message semantics, and users/deadline usage. ``` Search completed: 5 queries executed, 50 documents found ``` # 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking **Core Requirements** 1. Task cards must surface more at‑a‑glance info: **pending messages**, **total messages**, **last update (relative time)**. 2. New‑task form: add a **ProjectDetailt** selector to assign the task to a project. 3. New‑task form: show an **avatar quick‑picks** row of recently‑used profiles. 4. Allow assigning a task to **one or more users**. 5. Allow setting a **deadline**. **Strategic Approach** - `SprintTaskCard.vue` renders each sprint task → add computed metadata (message count, pending = `done === false`, `moment().fromNow()`) plus assignees / deadline / project chips. - `SprintBoardModals.vue` owns the "New Task" form → extend `newTask` model with `project_id`, `users`, `deadline`; reuse the existing `ProjectDetailt.vue`, derive recent profiles from `$storex.chats.allChats`, inject a multi‑user dropdown and a date input. - `SprintBoardView.vue` forwards the create event → pass the new fields through, then persist the extended metadata via the existing `chats.updateChatInfo` action (which already round‑trips sprint fields such as `sprints`). This keeps the change inside the provided working files and avoids duplicating the large sprint store. **Dependencies & Risks** - The store action `kanban.newSprintTask` destructures a fixed set of fields, so extra keys are ignored on create → we persist them with a follow‑up `updateChatInfo({ updates })` (safe: `project_id`/`users`/`deadline` survive exactly like `sprints`/`status` do today). - `users` already exists on the `Chat` model (`users: string[]`); `deadline` is a new top‑level key stored through the shared metadata endpoint. - `SprintTaskCard` referenced `this.$storex.planning.priorityConfig`; `planning` is not a registered store module — guard it so a task carrying `priority` cannot throw. **Target Files** | File | Role | | :-- | :-- | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintTaskCard.vue` | Card info (messages, pending, time, assignees, deadline, project) | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue` | Create form (project, recent profiles, assignees, deadline) | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardView.vue` | Persist extra metadata on create | --- # 2. Minimum Changes Approach - **SprintTaskCard.vue** – add `moment` import; keep existing structure; insert a "meta row" (project / assignees / deadline) and enrich the footer with message + pending + relative‑time indicators; add corresponding computeds; guard `priority`. - **SprintBoardModals.vue** – add `ProjectDetailt` import + `loadUsers` on mount; extend `DEFAULT_NEW_TASK`; add Project, Recent‑profiles, Assignees and Deadline controls to the New Task modal only (Add‑existing modal untouched); extend `confirmNewTask` payload; add supporting computeds/methods. - **SprintBoardView.vue** – extend `onTaskCreated` to persist `project_id`, `users`, `deadline` after `newSprintTask`. Validation before proceeding is welcome — each section is independent. --- # 3. File changes ```vue src/components/kanban/board/SprintTaskCard.vue ``` | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintTaskCard.vue` | Modify | ` ``` | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue` | Modify | ` ``` | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardView.vue` | Modify | `methods.onTaskCreated` | Split `project_id`/`users`/`deadline` from the create payload and persist them via `$storex.chats.updateChatInfo` after `newSprintTask` | --- # 4. File Change Summary | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintTaskCard.vue` | Modify | card template + computeds | Shows project, assignees (avatar group), deadline badge, message count, pending count, relative last‑update time | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue` | Modify | New Task modal + logic | Adds ProjectDetailt selector, recent‑profile avatar quick picker, multi‑user assignee picker, deadline input with quick presets | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardView.vue` | Modify | `onTaskCreated` | Persists `project_id`, `users`, `deadline` on the created task | **Notes / follow‑ups** - `users` already exists on the `Chat` model; `deadline` is stored as a top‑level chat key through the same metadata path used today for `sprints`/`status`, so it round‑trips like those do. - "Pending messages" is defined as messages with `done === false` (an assistant answer still streaming/queued) — the only reliably client‑available notion of “pending”. If your backend exposes an unread counter, the `pendingCount` computed is the single place to swap it in: `src/components/kanban/board/SprintTaskCard.vue → computed.pendingCount`. - `SprintTaskCard.priority` was guarded against the unregistered `planning` store to prevent a runtime throw on tasks carrying a `priority` value.
